hints: Think about changing the conditions around the enemy.
A grower might arrange for help when the weather will not provide it.
Nine letters: describes land after water has been supplied to it.
arid-irrigated.explanation: Supplying land with water directly counters its lack of rainfall or moisture.

hints: Think about the quality a careful investigator wants in an account.
What matters is whether it is grounded in what actually happened.
Eleven letters, ending NESS: the quality of being based on facts.
false-factualness.explanation: Being actual and based on fact is the opposite of being false.

hints: Think about what could get a stalled effort going again.
It needs a fresh supply of energy or enthusiasm.
Twelve letters, a verb beginning RE: give something renewed vitality.
inert-reinvigorate.explanation: Giving renewed energy or vitality counters being slow and apathetic.

hints: Imagine finding something neglected that is still worth saving.
A skilled craftsperson could bring it back towards its former condition.
Eleven letters: the name for that process of bringing something back.
rot-restoration.explanation: Bringing something back into good condition counters its decay.

hints: Think of the feeling after the pressure of a long day begins to lift.
A slower pace and a few deep breaths could help.
8 letters: ending ING: making someone less tense or stressed.
anger-relaxing.explanation: Making someone calmer and less tense counters anger.

hints: Think about how a careful listener might test a claim.
An independent check could establish whether it is true.
10 letters: ending ABLE: capable of being checked for truth.
lie-verifiable.explanation: A claim that can be checked against facts counters an unsupported falsehood.

hints: Picture someone facing a daunting situation without shrinking back.
The word names a quality, rather than a brave action.
12 letters: ending NESS: the quality of being unafraid.
fear-fearlessness.explanation: An absence of fear directly counters being afraid.

hints: Think of many separate parts working towards one coherent result.
A conductor does it for musicians; a planner can do it for an event.
12 letters: a past-tense verb meaning arranged and coordinated carefully.
chaos-orchestrated.explanation: Coordinating the parts of an activity brings order to chaos.

hints: Think about a different approach to sharing what you have.
Picture giving freely, without holding anything back.
Twelve letters, ending LY: describes giving without limiting the amount.
stingy-unstintingly.explanation: Giving freely, without restricting the amount, is the opposite of being unwilling to give.

hints: Think of something tired or neglected getting a fresh start.
It has been given new energy and purpose.
11 letters: beginning RE: given fresh life or vigour.
Think about what makes someone a reliable witness.
It is a quality of an honest account, rather than a particular fact.
12 letters: ending NESS: the quality of telling things as they really are.
untruth-truthfulness.explanation: Honesty and conformity to facts counter an untrue statement.

hints: Imagine someone with the power to punish choosing a gentler response.
They show compassion and spare unnecessary suffering.
10 letters: ending LY: in a way that shows mercy.
Think of a conversation in which nothing is hidden between the lines.
Someone says what they mean, frankly and without evasion.
10 letters: ending NESS: the quality of being straightforward.
deceit-directness.explanation: Being frank and straightforward counters deception.

hints: Picture a mood where little things no longer feel so serious.
There is room for playfulness and carefree laughter.
12 letters: a single adjective meaning cheerful and carefree.
rage-lighthearted.explanation: A cheerful, carefree mood counters fury.

hints: Picture a person drawn towards a challenge that others shy away from.
Danger can feel exciting to this person.
9 letters: a noun for a recklessly bold or adventurous person.
dread-daredevil.explanation: Boldly facing danger counters shrinking from it in dread.

hints: Imagine choosing the room with the most energy in it.
The answer compares several things and picks the most animated.
9 letters: ending IEST: the most full of life and activity.
Picture a jumble in which everything now has a clear place.
Someone has organised it according to a consistent method.
12 letters: ending IZED: arranged according to a system.
Think about making a surface safe after contamination.
This could be applied to kill harmful germs.
12 letters: a substance that prevents infection by destroying microbes.
Think of the step between hearing a claim and accepting it as true.
Someone checks it against evidence.
12 letters: ending ATION: the process of confirming accuracy or truth.
fictive-verification.explanation: Checking a claim against facts counters a deceptive invention.

hints: Think of the energy someone brings to a performance.
Their manner is vigorous and full of enthusiasm.
8 letters: an adjective meaning lively and full of energy.
Think of what turns an uncertain claim into an established fact.
Independent evidence backs up that it really happened.
12 letters: ending ATION: the act of establishing that something is true.
fiction-confirmation.explanation: Establishing what is true counters a deliberately false account.

hints: Think about how someone responds when another person is suffering.
They care about the pain and want to relieve it.
13 letters: an adjective meaning showing sympathy and concern for others.
spite-compassionate.explanation: Concern for another person’s suffering counters a wish to hurt them.

hints: Think of what people bring to a shared effort.
Money, time or useful work can all count.
13 letters: a plural noun for things given towards a common purpose.
stint-contributions.explanation: Giving towards a shared purpose counters holding back.

hints: Think about the basis on which a claim should be described.
The description follows the evidence, rather than an invented account.
9 letters: ending LY: in a way that is based on facts.
fallacy-factually.explanation: Grounding a statement in facts counters a false belief.

hints: Imagine a frosty meeting taking on a warmer tone.
Someone becomes more welcoming and well disposed towards others.
10 letters: ending IER: more characteristic of a friend.
ire-friendlier.explanation: A more friendly attitude counters anger and hostility.

hints: Think of the effect a steady voice can have on a frightened crowd.
Someone is soothing agitation and restoring calm.
9 letters: ending ING: bringing someone into a peaceful, calmer state.
panic-pacifying.explanation: Soothing fear and agitation counters panic.

hints: Think of many people working together without getting in one another’s way.
Someone needs to organise their different actions into a shared plan.
10 letters: a verb meaning bring different activities into organised cooperation.
riot-coordinate.explanation: Organising people’s actions into cooperation counters disorder.

hints: Picture a damaged thing being made useful again.
It has been built back up from what remained.
13 letters: beginning RE and ending ED: built again after damage or destruction.
rotten-reconstructed.explanation: Rebuilding something damaged counters its deterioration.

hints: Imagine a stalled effort after a fresh burst of enthusiasm.
It has been given renewed strength and energy.
11 letters: ending ATED: filled with fresh vigour.
inertia-invigorated.explanation: Renewed energy counters inactivity and reluctance to move.

hints: Think of what a detective needs before deciding what really happened.
It provides a basis for believing or rejecting a claim.
8 letters: a noun for facts or information supporting a conclusion.
deceive-evidence.explanation: Facts that establish what happened counter deception.
